title: Heuristic Shape Registrar and Ingest Gateway
creator: Maya Ortiz
description:
Problem: Console usage events are increasingly heterogeneous as new SDKs and clients emit slightly different shapes (missing fields, renamed keys, typed strings for numeric fields). Strict schema rejection creates operational load and customer support tickets; overly permissive ingestion masks regressions and causes downstream analytics drift.

Goal: Build a resilient ingest gateway that registers and tracks event shape variants, applies heuristic validation (shape similarity, value pattern checks, field inference), and provides progressive normalization while preserving raw payloads for audit and debug. The service should reduce hard rejections by at least 80% for benign deviations while surfacing potential regressions to ops/PM.

Scope and deliverables:
- Ingest Gateway (edge service) that accepts telemetry events, performs fast heuristic checks, and tags events with a shape_id.
- Shape Registrar: lightweight registry that stores observed shape fingerprints, example payloads, and stability metadata (first_seen, last_seen, acceptance_policy).
- Normalization pipelines: a set of idempotent normalizers applied by shape_id that perform safe transforms (coerce numeric strings, canonicalize timestamps, fill known legacy keys).
- Validation policy engine: rules for hard reject vs accept-with-warn vs normalize-and-accept; configurable per project/team via Console.
- Telemetry / metrics: ingestion success rate, p95 latency, percent normalized, schema drift alerts, unique shape count growth.
- Retention: keep raw event in cold storage (S3) for 90 days; normalized event flows to analytics topic.

Key non-goals: full-featured schema registry with Avro/Protobuf enforcement is out of scope for this ticket; we will integrate with that separately if needed. This is not a replacement for formal contract management between services.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ingest Gateway handles current peak traffic with <50ms p95 validation latency in staging.
- Default policy reduces hard rejections on historical sample by >=80% while keeping false-accept rate <0.5% (measured against curated eval set).
- Shape Registrar provides an API to list shapes, examples, and acceptance policy and is viewable in Console (read-only) for PM/SEs.
- End-to-end integration test and canary rollout plan documented.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Heuristic checks will use deterministic rules (regex, type coercion, presence/absence heuristics) to stay debuggable; we may add a lightweight ML-based classifier in a follow-up if heuristics prove insufficient.
- We intentionally store raw events to avoid irreversible normalization; normalized events will carry provenance metadata (shape_id, normalizer_version).
- To avoid adding latency on hot paths, normalization will be a two-phase process: fast, safe transforms at ingest; optional deeper normalization asynchronously for complex repairs.
- Failure modes: gateway throttling -> failover to passthrough mode with logging and metric spike; normalization bug -> ability to replay raw events and reprocess with a new normalizer.

Rollout and observability:
- Feature flag gated on per-customer basis; start with internal teams and small PLG cohort.
- Metrics to monitor: ingest_latency_p95, ingest_rejection_rate, normalized_rate, unique_shapes_7d, replay_backlog_size.
- Alerts: >0.5% sudden increase in rejection rate, unique_shapes daily growth >300% for a project, replay backlog >100k.

Docs and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Heuristic+Shape+Registrar+Design
- API spec: https://docs.redwood-inference.com/console/internal/shape-registrar-api
- Implementation PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4532 (gateway), https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4638 (registrar)
- Load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ingest/shape-registrar-load

Longer-term considerations:
- Integrate with a formal schema registry and open-source parsers (Avro/Protobuf) for binary schemas.
- Add a human-in-the-loop UI for approving new shapes and pinning acceptance policies.
- Expand heuristics to detect subtle semantic changes (units change, enum drift) using labeled prompt sets and periodic evaluations.
comments: 2026-01-12 - Arjun: Initial spike complete. Proof-of-concept gateway accepts sample events, computes Murmur3 shape fingerprint. Observed 12 distinct variants for the /usage/submit event during 24h internal traffic.

2026-01-18 - Maya: Reviewed design doc with PMs; agreed default acceptance policy: accept-with-warn for benign coercions; hard reject for missing primary identifiers (user_id/project_id). Follow-ups: list of primary identifiers per event type needed.

2026-01-25 - Priya (SRE): Load test (stage) at 1.5x traffic shows p95 validation latency ~46ms, CPU spike on gateway container due to regex cost. Action: micro-optimizations and precompiled regex cache.

2026-01-30 - Arjun: Implemented two-phase normalization. Quick-path normalization applied on hot path; complex transforms pushed to async rewriter job. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4532
2026-02-02 - QA: Built replay harness and ran against 7-day raw sample. Normalization reduced hard rejects from 3.8% -> 0.4% for target events. QA to create regression test suite for new normalizers.
2026-02-04 - PM (Lina): Prioritizing shape-approval UI in next cycle to allow product teams to pin acceptance policies. Added as follow-up: PM-4122.
2026-02-05 - Arjun: Updated acceptance criteria and added canary rollout plan. Next: security review for raw payload cold-store access control.
tests: unit: shape fingerprinting edge cases (empty keys, nested objects)
integration: end-to-end ingest -> normalize -> analytics topic write
load: 2x production sustained for 10m with p95 < 60ms
